advances: A sufficient bound at one chosen actual integer anchor with explicit accounting of unused original mass.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
For each pair use 793210f8a4be3647 (1) at coefficients $1/2$, and scale its uniform-marginal coupling to mass $t_j$. The resulting midpoint law is supported in $K_p$ with density at most $t_j/((a_j^{1/d}+b_j^{1/d})/2)^d$. Summing gives a measure $\eta\le L\mathbf1_{K_p}\,dx$ of mass $T$, hence $\alpha\le L$. Distinct pairs use disjoint endpoints and the scaled marginals are bounded by the original endpoint volumes, so $R\ge0$. The integer coordinate of the allocated centroid is $p$, and by linearity of the midpoint the continuous coordinate is the centroid of $\mathbf1_{K_p}\,dx+2\eta$, which lies in the interior of $K_p$. The midpoint indicator of any closed cap is at most the sum of its two endpoint indicators. Thus the original captured mass is at least the sum of the own-fiber cap volume and the midpoint trace mass. This use of marginal masses is separate from the density ceiling; no product of endpoint weights enters.

Tighten a containing cap to pass through $Y$. For a nonzero continuous normal apply the same-batch arbitrary-ceiling saturation bound to that trace. A pure-base through-cap contains the whole own fiber and at least one endpoint per pair, so its original mass is at least $k+T$. The normalized saturation bound also equals $\Gamma_d(1+L)[1-2\delta/(1+2\alpha)]-\delta\le(1+L)-\delta=1+\alpha$, so this case gives at least the required mass as well. Compare the established depth to $\Gamma_d M/2^n$ using $M/k=1+2\alpha+R/k$ to get the allowance. For $L\ge1$ and $\delta\le1/8$, the strict margin $E_d>1/44$ applies. Also $\Gamma_d\le1/2$ by the binomial inequality, giving the stated dimension-independent allowance at $n=1$.

In the final specialization choose $t_j=v_j$ for every pair. The compatible midpoint contains the interpolation of the two endpoint bodies and lies in $K_p$, so Brunn–Minkowski gives $v_j\le k$. Here $L=m$, $\delta=\sum_j(1-v_j/k)$ and $R=0$. The allocation is the entire original positive-volume measure, so the bound applies to the full centroid and is strictly above $\Gamma_d M/2+k/44$.
statement:
Let $K_p$ be an actual integer fiber of volume $k>0$ of a convex body in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $n,d\ge1$, with original mixed volume $M$. For distinct reflected endpoint pairs about $p$ of positive volumes $a_j,b_j$, choose equal masses $0\le t_j\le\min(a_j,b_j)$ from the two uniform endpoint measures. Put
$$
T=\sum_j t_j,\quad L=\sum_j\frac{t_j}{((a_j^{1/d}+b_j^{1/d})/2)^d},
\quad \alpha=T/k,\quad\delta=L-\alpha,\quad R=M-k-2T .
$$
Under $2\delta\le d(1+2\alpha)$ the centroid $Y$ of the allocation (the whole own fiber and the indicated endpoint fractions) lies at base $p$ in the actual own fiber and has raw depth at least $k[\Gamma_d(1+2\alpha)/2+E_d(L,\delta)]$, with
$$
E_d(L,\delta)=\frac{\Gamma_d}{2}-\delta\left[1-\Gamma_d+
\frac{2\Gamma_d(1+L)}{1+2L-2\delta}\right],
\qquad \Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d .
$$
Consequently $R/k\le(2^{n-1}-1)(1+2\alpha)+2^nE_d(L,\delta)/\Gamma_d$ suffices for the original target $\Gamma_dM/2^n$. If $L\ge1$ and $\delta\le1/8$, replacing $E_d$ by $1/44$ makes the target comparison strict. In particular when $n=1$ this allows $R\le k/(22\Gamma_d)$ and hence $R\le k/11$ suffices. If all positive fibers form $m\ge1$ reflected pairs together with $K_p$, each pair having equal endpoint volumes $v_j$ with $\sum_j(1-v_j/k)\le1/8$, then the actual full mixed centroid has raw depth strictly greater than $\Gamma_d M/2+k/44$, regardless of the endpoint shapes.
title: Actual reflected-pair allocations with a saturation margin and unused-mass allowance
